council: Vale of White Horse District Council
current_evidence: Could not confirm. The shared WebFetch budget ran out before the council's 'Validation checklists' page or the guide could be read, and the web search budget ran out too. Search results show the council's validation checklists page (whitehorsedc.gov.uk ... /validation-check-lists) but no newer guide than the June 2024 one, so Grokbot's link is plausibly current but unverified.

issues.detail: Grokbot mixed in content from the superseded January 2023 guide (2023-01-31-Final-Validation-Guide.pdf) alongside the June 2024 guide. Most tab items come from the 2023 guide: drawing standards, the checklist explanation, file-size and single-page PDF rules, GDPR text, and the nutrient neutrality text. So do the Full planning 'Ecological Survey' trigger and the Full planning 'Street scene' row. These should be re-sourced from the current guide.

'Health Impact Assessment' is listed as a Vale requirement under Full planning, but the guide is a joint South Oxfordshire/Vale document and marks this item 'SOUTH REQUIREMENT ONLY'. The 'Energy / Sustainability Statement' trigger quotes only South Oxfordshire policy (SOLP 2035 DES10), so whether it applies in the Vale needs checking.
issues.evidence: HIA trigger: '7.28 Health Impact Assessment (HIA) SOUTH REQUIREMENT ONLY'; Energy trigger: 'The policy requirement for this is set out in SOLP 2035 policy DES10'

issues.detail: Requirements whose own trigger says 'all major planning application proposals' are placed only under Full planning, and Outline gets only Street scene and the checklist form. Examples are Air Quality, Archaeology, Ecology, Landscape plans, S106 Heads of Terms, SCI and Retail impact. Outline (major) applications should carry them as well. More than 20 rows carry the 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning' note, e.g. Affordable Housing, Arboricultural, Contaminated Land, Flood Risk, Noise, Transport and Waste.
issues.evidence: SCI trigger: 'A statement of community involvement is required for: all major planning application proposals (residential and non-residential)'

issues.detail: The 'Change of use - prior approval' row says '(none)', but Grokbot's own nutrient neutrality text says a Nutrient Neutrality Statement is needed for 'barn/building conversions to dwellings including Prior Approval proposals' within the SAC nutrient catchment. Householder rows also leave out drawing items the guide applies where relevant: roof plans where the roof form changes, and site sections and levels on sloping sites.
issues.evidence: tab_items: '- new homes - barn/building conversions to dwellings including Prior Approval proposals - student accommodation - care homes...'

issues.detail: The Economic Report (7.24) has no row of its own. Its trigger ('all changes of use of employment land ... where no equivalent replacement employment') ended up as the trigger of a 'Pre-application advice' row instead.
issues.evidence: Pre-application row trigger: '...7.24 Economic Report 7.24.1 An Economic Report is required for: - all changes of use of employment land (either current or last use)...'

issues.detail: Several triggers are spliced from the wrong section or cut off. 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' quotes the retail sequential and impact test (7.34), not flood. 'Habitats Regulations Assessment' quotes the ecology survey trigger. 'Flood Risk Assessment' and 'Energy' quote each other's section text. 'Retail Impact Assessment' stops at 'in Vale of White Horse:' before giving the Vale threshold. 'Planning Statement' is just 'an overarching Planning Statement.' 'Biodiversity Net Gain' gives no trigger at all.
issues.evidence: Retail trigger ends '...Outside of town centres and local centres (as defined in policy TC2 of SOLP 2035), proposals for 500sqm or more in Vale of White Horse:'

issues.detail: Several tab items are process text rather than requirements: the 21-day/7-day invalid-application follow-up and the Validation Disputes procedure, the GDPR personal data text, the explanation that the checklist is 'a double-check mechanism', and page-header fragments such as 'P a g e 8 | 32 Planning Application Validation Requirements'. Advert and LDC rows also cite bare checklist headings ('Local List Requirements In addition to the national requirements set out above...') as triggers for national drawings.
issues.evidence: tab_items under 'Submission rules' and 'Local forms / checklists'

issues.detail: 'All plans to be submitted as separate single page PDF files' / 'Multiple pages, combined PDF files will not be accepted' is captured three times (twice from the 2023 guide, once from the 2024 guide). The nutrient neutrality scope list is captured twice, once from each guide version.
issues.evidence: tab_items Submission rules rows 'P a g e 8 | 32' and 'P a g e 8 | 33'

issues.detail: The single 'Lawful development cert' category merges the CLUED (existing) and CLOPUD (proposed) checklists. Sworn statements and affidavits and the photographic record apply only to existing-use (CLUED) applications. Several type-specific checklists used are older December 2022 versions from 2023/03 uploads (Householder, LBC, Advert, RM, s73, NMA, PiP), so whether newer checklists exist should be checked.
issues.evidence: Lawful development rows sourced from both FINAL-CLUED and FINAL-CLOPUD checklists; triggers ending 'December 2022'

summary: Neither the Vale guide nor the council page could be re-fetched because the WebFetch and search budgets ran out, so currency of the June 2024 joint guide is unverified. Grokbot's own extracts show it mixed in the superseded 2023 guide, assigned a South Oxfordshire-only requirement (HIA) to the Vale, spliced several triggers from the wrong sections and left 'all major' items off Outline.

withdrawn_issues.detail: The List date 2024-06-01 comes from the upload-month folder in the URL ('Date basis: url path'), not from text in the document. The filename itself gives 4 June 2024. The date stated inside the guide should be checked and used instead.
withdrawn_issues.evidence: reference_row 'Date basis: url path (upload month)'; filename '2024-06-04-Final-Validation-Guide-1.pdf'
withdrawn_issues.grok_comment: The basis label is the URL path, as the audit says, but the guide cover itself reads "A GUIDE TO SUBMITTING PLANNING APPLICATIONS ... June 2024", so the 2024-06-01 list date matches the document text.
withdrawn_issues.claude_response: Accepted. The workbook stores list dates to the month, so the value is right; only the date-basis label could be better. Not a Grokbot error.
